summary: A successful force bolt cast crosses the Wizard’s next spell-skill practice threshold. C weapon.c:use_skill() calls give_may_advance_msg(), which displays “You feel more confident in your spell casting skills.” and then calls handle_tip(TIP_ENHANCE). JavaScript use_skill() updates practice but skips the notification through note_unported(), so the recorded message screen is absent. handle_tip(TIP_ENHANCE) is already implemented; the repair must preserve its source order after the message.

source.branch: use_skill(skill, degree) changes P_ADVANCE only for a non-P_NONE, unrestricted skill and calls give_may_advance_msg(skill) only when the practice change makes can_advance() become true. add_weapon_skill(n) calls give_may_advance_msg(P_NONE) only when adding slots increases the count of currently advanceable skills. The helper prints a category-specific confidence message and then calls handle_tip(TIP_ENHANCE), discarding its boolean result.

evidence: The saved admitted v65 evaluation and .cache/current-work-queue.json entry identify synthetic/v65/v65-spell-practice-action2, 603 recorded steps, 601/603 screens, 4369/4369 RNG calls, and 602/603 cursors. The first mismatch is segment 0 step 529, key h, at row 0 column 0: C shows Y and JavaScript shows T; there is no RNG mismatch at that step.

The retained session recording challenges/cases/v65/v65-spell-practice-action2.session.json shows step 528 selecting force bolt, with prompt “In what direction?”, and step 529 displaying “You feel more confident in your spell casting skills.--More--” in C after direction h. Its step 528/529 RNG entries are attributed to spell.c:spelleffects_check, attrib.c:exercise, and zap.c:weffects; the relevant message is the post-cast skill notification rather than a new random branch.

Upstream spell.c:1599 calls use_skill(skill, spellev(spell)) after a successful non-forced spell. weapon.c:1424-1434 increments P_ADVANCE and calls give_may_advance_msg only when the increase newly makes can_advance true. weapon.c:76-84 formats the message as “spell casting skills” for spell skills and follows it with handle_tip(TIP_ENHANCE).

JavaScript spell.js:1938 already calls use_skill after a successful cast. In js/weapon.js:1921-1927, use_skill updates the skill record but replaces the C notification with note_unported; add_weapon_skill has a second placeholder at js/weapon.js:1937-1947. js/hack.js:622-650 already implements handle_tip(TIP_ENHANCE), so its return may be ignored while preserving the printed tip when enabled.

Upstream callers of the source functions include spell.c:spelleffects, uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon_dmg_recalc, dokick.c:dokick, steed.c:exercise_steed and hack.c:domove_core for use_skill; attrib.c:adjabil and pray.c:gcrownu call add_weapon_skill. JavaScript has an existing adjabil call, while gcrownu remains an explicit note_unported gap in js/pray.js. The eventual async notification must be awaited through implemented JavaScript caller paths to keep the source message before subsequent game output.
